text: 015-D SPIKE COMPLETE (2026-07-29, live/hands-on, post-104-F main 00665738) - daemon 'engram index' cross-file singleton non-persist + CLI response hang. Both symptoms reproduced live: the IPC hang (>270s) is DAEMON/IPC-path-specific (in-process --direct returns ~1s) with H2 confirmed as the mechanism (synchronous long-op response + daemon-spawn/model-load OUTSIDE the client request timeout); the cross-file alpha->beta singleton is ABSENT from the persisted resolved graph (non-persist corroborated; H1 commit-boundary / H4 post-pass-not-invoked OPEN). 104-F does NOT fix it (different layer). Prior direct.rs:162 hypothesis REFUTED. FOLLOW-UP = Ship-owned/instrumented runtime-verification spike: single pre-warmed daemon + validated corpus, trace post-pass invocation/commit boundary + IPC framing to PIN the root cause, then author a fail-safe fix. Do NOT fabricate a fix on an unproven root cause (013-D discipline). Repro procedure + candidate fix directions: docs/decisions/2026-07-29-daemon-index-ipc-hang-spike-findings.md. Deliberation 015-D. [STAGE cycle-5 2026-07-30 NON-FOLD DISPOSITION: NOT folded into feature 105-F. Root cause is DISTINCT from 105.003-T/7A317008 -- 015-D's fresh-workspace unique-def corpus has no duplicate-callee/excluded-file trigger for the R3 ordering bug; 015-D non-persist mechanism remains UNPINNED (013-D discipline); IPC-hang portion is out-of-width (architectural async response). Remains ACTIVE; deferred to a Ship-owned runtime-verification spike. Traceability: related_to links 105-F->015-D and 105.003-T->015-D; full rationale in the 015-D comment log + docs/exec-plans/2026-07-30-daemon-sync-index-reconciliation-plan.md. REVISIT if the runtime spike pins non-persist to the same post-pass/commit boundary R3 touches.]

cozo 0.8+ major-version bump to clear the remaining lz4_flex RUSTSEC-2026-0041 advisory (the 1 accepted cargo-audit finding from 102-F). Path: cozo -> swapvec (non-optional cozo dep, pins lz4_flex ^0.10, cannot be feature-dropped like the requests->minreq path). No in-range fix exists at cozo 0.7.6; requires a cozo 0.8+ major bump with graph-backend blast-radius (storage-sqlite/graph-algo API surface). Accepted-with-rationale in docs/decisions/2026-07-28-cargo-audit-advisory-triage.md: swapvec is cozo internal disk-spill (trusted round-trip data, not attacker-controlled). Revisit when cozo publishes 0.8+ or when a patched lz4_flex 0.10.x lands.

Periodic trigger check: swapvec or cozo re-pins lz4_flex >=0.11.6, OR a patched lz4_flex 0.10.x backport lands in-range for swapvec 0.3's ^0.10 constraint. Distinct from 99AFF44B/017-D (the heavyweight cozo 0.8+ major bump = Option A). Check via cargo update --dry-run / cargo audit + swapvec/cozo release notes. Refs: docs/decisions/2026-07-28-cargo-audit-advisory-triage.md, docs/decisions/2026-07-29-cozo-0_8-major-bump-feasibility-deliberation.md.

PR#301 review follow-up (099.004-T, src/services/parsing/python.rs:329): qualified staging via python_local promotes calls through is_qualified, attributing callers by first-match find_function_id (code_graph.rs:1767,:2830). Duplicate top-level caller names in one file can stage under an arbitrary duplicate while trusting the canonical target, minting a wrong-origin edge; the bare-call path fails closed via find_unique_function_id. Add ambiguity-aware caller attribution (or preserve the fail-closed check) for qualified staging plus a duplicate-caller regression test. Defensible under 014-D first-match design but a narrow correctness gap.

PR#301 review follow-up (105-F sync/index domain, src/services/code_graph.rs:1335): the index path unconditionally publishes the current topology snapshot even when result.errors holds a transient per-file read failure. A topology-forced descendant that fails to read keeps its old canonical path while the snapshot is published; the next ordinary index sees no topology change and hash-skips the unchanged file, so cleanup is missed. Preserve the absent/old snapshot when a topology-forced file fails, or persist an explicit retry set.

PR#301 review follow-up (105-F sync/index domain, src/services/code_graph.rs:2397,:1537): 099.005-T repaired only the sync path. A non-forced index_workspace parses an empty file, deletes its function metadata, and retracts old 'direct' edges only when force=true; if any other file is hash-skipped the later dangling-edge sweep is also skipped, so the emptied file's raw direct edges survive an ordinary index. Add the same empty-file eviction to the index path plus an index regression with another unchanged file.

PR#301 review follow-up (015-D durable-knowledge accuracy): symptom-1 cross-file singleton non-persist is labeled CORROBORATED in the spike findings frontmatter/summary, but caveat #2 states the known-good --direct path also produced no alpha->beta edge and the minimal corpus was never validated against a known-GREEN singleton. Soften to 'inconclusive pending corpus validation' across docs/decisions/2026-07-29-daemon-index-ipc-hang-spike-findings.md, docs/memory/2026-07-29/stage-cycle4-held-items-memory.md, .backlogit/stash.jsonl, .backlogit/memories.json, and .backlogit/queue/015-D.md; make known-GREEN corpus validation the prerequisite before any persist/non-persist follow-up.

Tighten R1/R2 (105-F) concurrency doc-comments in src/server/state.rs: (1) PendingSyncState::publish doc claims the current generation is 'captured under the same lock' but current_sync_generation() is read via the sync_generation atomic OUTSIDE the pending_sync mutex CS (set_pending_sync ~L570, publish ~L599, arm setters); the tag is correct on reachable paths but for defense-in-depth read sync_generation INSIDE the PendingSyncState critical section and correct the comment. (2) The R2 publish_pending_sync_and_try_reacquire lost-wakeup proof comment (~L627) derives 'P2 happens-before chk' by treating a SeqCst total-order edge as a happens-before edge, which is not valid; the conclusion is correct via the pending_sync mutex critical-section order (chk reads false => chk CS precedes P2 CS => store(false) sb chk hb P2 sb P3 => P3 observes indexing==false and re-acquires). Restate the proof in terms of mutex CS ordering; note the indexing flag would be correct even at Relaxed so SeqCst is sufficient. Source: 105-F Concurrency Reviewer P3 advisories. Doc/robustness only; R1/R2 are functionally correct as written (no P0/P1).

R1 follow-up (105-F residual): coordinate the sync-generation transition with the binding publication AND the pending-sync publish so a producer cannot tag/coalesce with a stale generation. Two confirmed races from PR #302 Copilot review: (T1, set_workspace lifecycle.rs ~165-187) set_workspace_and_config publishes the new (workspace,config) binding BEFORE begin_scan_generation() bumps sync_generation; a concurrent sync_workspace in that window reads the new binding, fails try_start_indexing on the OLD hydration's lock, and publishes pending-sync tagged with the OLD generation, which the old hydration's cancel-path clear_pending_sync_for_generation(old_gen) then wipes -- the exact loss R1 targets, unexercised by the current tests (they advance generation before publishing). (T3, state.rs publish_pending_sync ~597) sync_generation is loaded OUTSIDE the pending_sync mutex, so an older-generation publish_pending_sync(revalidate) that captured gen G, paused across a rebind to G+1 and a newer routine publish (owner G+1), then resumed, OR-coalesces its REVALIDATE bit into the G+1 routine queue (G<=owner => publish else-branch) -- leaking an old generation's heavy companion into a new routine sync (the reverse ordering the 'newer replaces older' guard does NOT cover). Fix: make the generation increment share the pending_sync synchronization/binding transition (bump under the same mechanism that publishes the binding + read generation at the publish linearization point) so stale-capture windows close; add regressions that pause between snapshot publication and cancellation, and between generation-load and publish. Consequence today: narrow, self-healing (new generation's own scan re-queues needed work; leak causes an unnecessary revalidation, not loss/corruption) -- non-P0/P1. SUPERSEDES doc-only follow-up 1E70A289.

R2 follow-up (105-F residual): route the startup-sync producer through the R2 backstop. try_start_startup_sync (src/daemon/ipc_server.rs ~1210) still uses the pre-R2 producer pattern -- try_start_indexing() then, on failure, set_pending_sync() with NO re-attempt -- so it retains the same producer/consumer lost-wakeup TOCTOU that 105.002-T closed for the sync_workspace producer: if the startup task is descheduled after the failed try while the holder releases and runs its final empty-queue peek, it resumes, sets the bit, and no finisher is guaranteed until an external index/sync/watcher tick. R2 (105.002-T) intentionally wired the minimal backstop (publish_pending_sync_and_try_reacquire) only into the sync_workspace drain-caller path (the 0B5AAAD2 site, lifecycle.rs:466); this sibling producer was out of that scope. Fix: change try_start_startup_sync to publish_pending_sync_and_try_reacquire and, on true (re-acquired => guaranteed finisher), finish_indexing + drain_pending_sync_to_completion for the startup sync; add a RED->GREEN test for the intent-after-final-peek interleaving on the startup path. Consequence today: latency/stall on daemon startup only, self-healed by the bounded drain loop + periodic watcher drains (not permanent loss) -- non-P0/P1. Source: PR #302 Copilot thread state.rs:572.

099-S/097.004-T W1 follow-up: lineage recall gap in resolve_cell_candidates (src/services/parsing/python.rs ~L1311/1333). Two fail-closed false-negatives from U2b invalidation: (1) read;write;read;write reuse (df=read(a);df.write(t1);df=read(b);df.write(t2)) drops the 2nd valid edge because WriteCall does not consume the binding, so the 2nd read looks like a double-read and invalidates; (2) invalidated_sessions is shared between session invalidation and re-read poison, so df=other;df=spark.read(a);df.write(t) drops a valid edge. Fix: dedicated re-read invalidation set (keep invalidated_sessions for session receivers only) + per-var written-since-bind flag so a re-read after a write rebinds instead of invalidating, without breaking single-read->multi-write fan-out. Precision floor unaffected (fail-closed). Add regression fixtures. Deferred from 099-S review gate.

099-S review nits (P3): (1) W2 resolve_table (src/models/lineage.rs ~L194) has dead-code branches name.contains('::') and name.starts_with(':') now unreachable after is_spark_unquoted_identifier restricts components to [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* — trim or annotate. (2) tests/integration/lineage_extractor_version_rollout_test.rs lacks a current-stamp->skip control assertion (ingested==0) between first index and rollback, to make the freshness gate self-contained rather than relying on notebook_lineage_freshness_test.rs. Deferred from 099-S review gate.

099-S/097.001-T V2 follow-up (precision): the comment-aware Spark INSERT normalizer in src/services/parsing/sql.rs has two rare fail-open edges against its no-rewrite contract. (1) skip_block_comment (~L480) returns at the FIRST inner '*/', but Spark 3.0+ supports nested bracketed comments (SPARK-28880); an INSERT ... TABLE after an inner '*/' but still inside the OUTER comment can be rewritten -> false-positive edge. Fix: track nesting depth, exit only when depth hits 0. (2) skip_line_comment (~L471) stops at every newline, but Spark SIMPLE_COMMENT continues a '--' comment across a line-ending backslash ('\\'+LF); an INSERT on the continued line can be rewritten. Fix: consume '\\'+LF continuations (LF only; CRLF ends the comment, matching Spark). Add nested-comment and backslash-continuation no-rewrite fixtures. Both are rare-input false-positive paths; deferred from 099-S review gate (Copilot suppressed comments, review-fix breaker reached).

Extend the shared fail-closed collected-set deletion reconciler (from 087.005.001-ST) to the pbip and backlog deletion sweeps (pbip_indexer.rs compute_deleted_paths L112 / sweep_deleted_pbip_files L857; backlog_indexer.rs compute_deleted_paths L49 / sweep_deleted_backlog_files L402). Same alias-backed stale-record vulnerability as notebook + non-TMDL PowerBI, but out of the 087.005/087.006 two-card freeze scope (plan-review P2-1). Do NOT bundle into 100-S.

087/100-S P2-1: PowerBI migration-window orphan content rows. On the first backfill after the powerbi_file_index_state marker was introduced, the marker map is empty so the non-TMDL hash-change delete (~powerbi_indexer.rs L1472) and TMDL dirty-scope pre-delete (~L1319) may leave orphan content rows briefly. Bounded and self-healing (next full-index pass rewrites), NOT data-loss. Consider a one-time backfill sweep or documenting the migration window.

087/100-S P3-1: out-of-bounds traversal root completeness. When collect_files_in_workspace_checked is called with a source_dir outside workspace_root, path-relativization can produce entries that the reconciler treats inconsistently. Largely masked by the P1-A fail-closed fix (3449a361) which now marks non-authoritative passes complete=false, but worth a dedicated guard/assert that the traversal root is within workspace_root. Low priority.

087/100-S P3-2: PowerBI content-record writes do not use the busy-retry helper. upsert_content_record / the atomic batch path in powerbi_indexer.rs write directly rather than through the busy-retry wrapper used elsewhere, so a transient cozo busy error surfaces as a hard failure instead of retrying. Consistency/robustness improvement, not a data-loss risk. Low priority.

087/100-S P2-3: source-removal marker hygiene. delete_powerbi_nodes_by_source removes nodes for a whole source but does not drop the corresponding powerbi_file_index_state markers, so a fully-removed source could leave stale markers. Adversarial review confirmed this fn currently has NO runtime call site (unreachable), so low priority — file for when a source-removal path is added.

087/100-S Copilot follow-up: the SHARED is_regular_file_in_workspace (source_traversal.rs) still fails OPEN on transient symlink_metadata/canonicalize errors (returns false -> treated as deleted). The 100-S reconciler now uses a dedicated fail-closed is_physically_absent, but the out-of-scope backlog_indexer.rs and pbip_indexer.rs compute_deleted_paths still call is_regular_file_in_workspace, so their deletion sweeps can wrongly delete a live record under an unreadable parent. Migrate those two callers to the fail-closed oracle (or harden the shared fn) once their sweeps are in scope. Same safety-floor class as 100-S.

087/100-S Copilot follow-up (test hardening): the marker-first delete ordering (P1-B) has no failure-path test. powerbi_sweep_drops_completion_marker_for_swept_paths only asserts final state and passes regardless of delete order, so it would not catch a P1-B regression. Add a fault-injection harness (failpoint/mock DB that aborts after the marker delete) and assert the next run reprocesses; cover all three delete paths (dirty-scope ~L1319, hash-change ~L1472, sweep ~L1624). Needs a fault-injection seam that does not exist yet, hence deferred from 100-S.

087/100-S Copilot follow-up (supersedes self-heal claim in A1BB7EB9): PowerBI marker migration window is NOT self-healing via the inline cleanup gates. On the first run after the powerbi_file_index_state relation is introduced the marker map is empty, so the dirty-scope and hash-change delete gates (which key off that map) are skipped; a file that had entities removed while the daemon was down keeps its stale entity rows, the marker is then written with the current hash, and later runs hash-skip it permanently. Not a safety-floor (never deletes live data) but leaves orphan rows. Add a one-time backfill: for content-record paths lacking a marker, run the stale-entity cleanup before writing the first marker.
